content.subsection: 4.1 Key steps in the diagnosis of chronic heart failure
content.summary: Diagnosis of chronic heart failure (CHF) requires symptoms and/or signs of HF plus objective evidence of cardiac dysfunction. Symptoms alone lack sufficient accuracy. Use BNP/NT-proBNP and echocardiography to confirm diagnosis and define phenotype based on LVEF.
content.signs_and_limitations: Symptoms and signs lack sufficient accuracy to be used alone to make the diagnosis of HF.
conditions_increasing_likelihood_of_CHF: Family history of cardiomyopathy (CMP) or sudden death

diagnostic_algorithm_highlights.initial_assessment: Suspect HF if risk factors, symptoms/signs, or abnormal ECG present.
diagnostic_algorithm_highlights.biomarkers: Measure NT-proBNP or BNP; thresholds cited (e.g. NT-proBNP ≥125 pg/mL or BNP ≥35 pg/mL) to proceed to echocardiography.
diagnostic_algorithm_highlights.imaging: Echocardiography to identify abnormal findings indicating cardiac dysfunction.
diagnostic_algorithm_highlights.phenotype_definition: If HF confirmed, define phenotype based on left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) measurement.

phenotype_thresholds.HFrEF: LVEF ≤40% (heart failure with reduced ejection fraction)
phenotype_thresholds.HFmrEF: LVEF 41–49% (heart failure with mildly reduced ejection fraction)
phenotype_thresholds.HFpEF: LVEF ≥50% (heart failure with preserved ejection fraction)

diagnostic_algorithm_highlights.next_steps: Determine aetiology and commence treatment if HF confirmed; consider other diagnoses if heart failure unlikely.

content.figure_legend_notes: Figure 1: Diagnostic algorithm for heart failure. Abbreviations explained include BNP (B-type natriuretic peptide), ECG (electrocardiogram), HFrEF, HFmrEF, HFpEF, LVEF, NT-proBNP (N-terminal pro-B type natriuretic peptide).
